tools.title: Add Coordinates
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Add or update shared parameters on selected or model-wide elements with project and survey coordinate values.
notes: Keep extension-root and `lib` bootstrap reliable before any coordinate logic runs. Preserve both selection-scoped and model-wide workflows. Report missing parameters or skipped elements explicitly rather than failing silently.

tools.title: MagpieGroup Data
tools.function:
Click: Copy the data from RBG_ConcStrength parameter into RBG_MagpieGroup parameter for all elements.
Shift+Click: Reset all RBG_MagpieGroup parameters to empty.
tools.purpose: Copy a chosen source parameter into `RBG_MagpieGroup` using a formatted token while preserving existing text.
inputs: Click: Copy the data from RBG_ConcStrength parameter into RBG_MagpieGroup parameter for all elements.
Shift+Click: Reset all RBG_MagpieGroup parameters to empty.
notes: Preserve existing text outside the managed token pattern. Keep unit handling compatible across older and newer Revit unit APIs. Limit edits to the targeted structural categories unless the workflow is intentionally expanded.

tools.title: PackageCreator Dockable Panel
tools.function: script.py startup.py
tools.purpose: Deliver a Revit dockable panel that reproduces as much practical functionality as possible from the standalone Issue Package Creator app while remaining native to pyRevit workflows. The panel must stay open while users continue modeling and provide live issue-package context for the active Revit project.
notes: Keep pushbutton script thin and delegate behavior to reusable library modules. Register and own dockable pane lifecycle centrally, not inside ad hoc UI handlers. Keep long-running or dependency-heavy operations out of WPF click handlers. Preserve audit-style outcomes: clear statuses, counts, warnings, and report paths. Treat CPython-only dependencies as helper-side concerns, not direct IronPython panel logic. Keep panel useful at narrow width and safe while user continues Revit work.

Start implementation with pane lifecycle and state contract, then wire actions one by one. Keep UI handlers thin and route all heavy operations through orchestrator methods. Preserve human-readable status and diagnostics from every helper action.

tools.location: RBG_SYD_Tools.tab > RBG Tools_Data.panel > DataStack2.stack > Transaction Logger.pushbutton
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Configure and toggle transaction logging for the active Revit session, either across the full model or targeted categories.
notes: Preserve the environment variable contract used by the logger startup flow. Keep readiness checks explicit so the tool fails clearly when startup support is not active. Distinguish full-model logging from targeted-category logging without mutating the underlying capture pipeline unexpectedly.

tools.title: Disallow Detach Elements
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Convert beam and wall joins to disallowed states and remove column attachments for targeted structural elements.
notes: Grouped elements remain a known limitation and should not be treated as safely editable. Preserve category-specific behavior for walls, framing, and columns. Any future unpin or regroup workflow should stay explicit and reversible.

tools.title: Elements by Level
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: List elements associated with a selected level, grouped by category and sorted by type, with linkified report output.
notes: Preserve the distinction between core model elements and optional view-specific or annotation elements. Keep grouping and type-name derivation resilient across element classes. Maintain report output as the primary user interaction surface.

tools.title: Quick Pin Categories
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Pin, unpin, or toggle pin state for selected categories across the model.
notes: Preserve worksharing and group-member checks before attempting mutation. Keep category scope explicit through the current category map. Treat groups and link instances as special cases rather than ordinary elements.

tools.title: RevClouds to Detail Groups
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Create detail-group equivalents of revision cloud linework for a selected revision and scope.
notes: Preserve the revision-to-cloud mapping and scope selection workflow. Keep worksharing and copy/paste safety checks intact before creating detail groups. Maintain style-selection behavior so generated detail linework remains readable.

tools.title: Slab Splitter
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Split one or more floors using mixed splitter elements and review or approve resulting parts.
notes: Preserve geometric tolerances and minimum size thresholds unless the behavior is intentionally recalibrated. Keep selection, geometric analysis, and replacement/approval decisions conceptually separate. Any document mutation path should stay transaction-safe and report failures clearly.

This tool currently embeds a large amount of UI and execution logic in one file; prefer extraction into `lib` for future refactors. If changing splitter interpretation, validate walls, framing, grids, columns, and floor-derived boundaries independently.

tools.title: Crop Views Quick Off
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Turn crop region visibility off for the active view or for all placed views on the active sheet.
notes: This tool only turns crop visibility off; do not broaden behavior accidentally. Preserve the distinction between active-sheet and single-view execution. Keep unsupported view handling explicit in the output rather than crashing the run.

tools.title:
Grids

tools.purpose: Set visible grids in the active view to 2D extents quickly.
inputs: Click: Set visible Grids in Active View to 2D (view-specific) extents.
notes: Only act on grids visible in the active printable view. Keep the current fast-path batch behavior and silent skip pattern for problematic grids unless diagnostics are intentionally added. Minimize regeneration and transaction overhead for large views.

tools.title:
Levels
2D / 3D
tools.function:

Shift+Click: Set them to 3D (model) extents.
tools.purpose: Set visible levels in the active section or elevation view to 2D extents.
inputs: Click: Set visible Levels in Active View to 2D (view-specific) extents.
notes: Restrict execution to printable section and elevation views. Preserve the low-overhead batch transaction pattern. Keep failure handling non-fatal per level so one problematic datum does not stop the run.

tools.title:
Levels: Head Switch
Left / Right

Shift+Click: Set them to Right Header only.

tools.title: Plan View Range Tool
tools.function: `script.py`
tools.purpose: Compare plan view range settings across multiple views and support controlled copying of those settings.
notes: Preserve formatting compatibility across differing Revit unit APIs. Keep comparison output aligned with the actual built-in parameters used for copy behavior. Treat view templates and template-controlled range settings as first-class constraints.

tools.title: Scope Box View Creation
tools.function: `script.py` `ViewCreator.xaml`
tools.purpose: Create and lay out views on sheets from a scope-box driven workflow with a WPF creator and selector interface.
notes: Do not mix static `ComboBoxItem` children with dynamic `ItemsSource` population. Keep view collection, preview, and creation/layout logic clearly separated. Protect transaction boundaries around any view or sheet mutation.

Read the XAML first, then trace event handlers and execution paths in `script.py`. If the workflow grows further, prefer extracting reusable creation logic into `lib` rather than adding more monolithic script code.

tools.title: Section Move
tools.function: `script.py` `DetailMoveWindow.xaml`
tools.purpose: Drive the DetailMove workflow for staging, previewing, and executing section or detail relocation tasks through a dedicated WPF window.
notes: Keep `script.py` as a thin launcher only. Preserve `StageMapRows` as the single vertical mapping panel model used by the UI. Keep UI-side execution aligned with the current in-window full run pattern and structured result payloads.

Start in `lib/detailmove_ui.py` for WPF behavior and `lib/detailmove_engine.py` for execution logic. UI changes should continue to surface run summaries without depending on pyRevit console-only output.
